structure.note: One class of common stock; 784,669,191 shares were outstanding on December 31, 2025, after about $4.7 billion of Boeing shares were issued for the Spirit AeroSystems acquisition (December 8, 2025). Boeing also has 5,750,000 shares of 6.00% Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock (aggregate liquidation preference $5,750 million), which convert into common stock by October 15, 2027. The proxy lists Vanguard, FMR and BlackRock as the holders above 5% of common stock.

notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. Sources: FY2025 Form 10-K (accession 0001628280-26-004357, filed January 30, 2026) and the 2026 proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0001193125-26-096787, filed March 6, 2026; principal shareholders as of the dates in its footnotes, share count at December 31, 2025). LEADER: David Calhoun ceased to be CEO on August 8, 2024 and retired from Boeing on March 1, 2025 (per the 2025 proxy, read for the prior edition). The 2026 proxy names him only as the prior CEO in the pay-versus-performance table; he is not a director or named executive officer and is not in its ownership tables, so status is no-reported-stake. 5% HOLDERS: Vanguard and FMR report holdings as of December 31, 2025; BlackRock's 6.8% rests on a filing as of December 31, 2024 and is stale. DIVIDENDS: no common dividends were paid in 2025 (suspended since 2020). The cash-flow statement shows $331 million of "Dividends paid on Mandatory convertible preferred stock" in 2025; that is a separate line for preferred holders, so it is excluded and dividends are recorded as 0. BUYBACKS: the quoted Item 5 footnote covers the fourth quarter; for the full year the cash-flow statement has no share repurchase line, and its $34 million "Employee taxes on certain share-based payment arrangements" is tax withholding, not a buyback. STOCK COMP: $426 million is the cash-flow add-back. GEOGRAPHY: the eight regional rows sum to the reported $89,463 million total; the 737 MAX concessions reconciling line has no 2025 amount.

footprint.notes: Employees by state are from Boeing's 'December 2025 Employment by Location' table on boeing.com/company, which matches the FY2025 year end; no newer edition found (checked 2026-11-24: the page still shows December 2025). It includes Spirit AeroSystems (acquisition completed Dec 8, 2025), which raises Kansas. The table names 10 states; 'Other U.S. States' (15,323) is an aggregate and is not mapped; 'Global' (25,371) is the non-U.S. total. The FY2025 10-K says the workforce was approximately 182,000 at Dec 31, 2025 with 14% outside the U.S.; nothing was derived from that split. Supplier spend by state: Boeing's per-state 'state cards' (boeing.com/.../state_cards/Card_XX.pdf) returned 404 for every state in the earlier research (not rechecked in this refresh), and the U.S. page gives only national figures, so no state supplier-spend rows are recorded. Sites: corporate HQ from the FY2025 10-K cover; the eight state 'key sites' cards from Boeing's U.S. page (still live, checked 2026-11-24) are state-level descriptions, not single facilities. The 10-K's Item 2 lists major locations (e.g. Greater Seattle, Wichita, Greater Charleston, Greater St. Louis) without figures.

paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (FY2025 Form 10-K, accession 0001628280-26-004357). Operating cash flow was small (1,065) after a further inventory build (1,501) and lower advances (−723), so paidOut (91.34bn) slightly exceeds revenue. The $9,672 million gain on dispositions (mainly the Digital Aviation Solutions divestiture) is not in revenue and is backed out of operating cash flow as a non-cash item; the $10,585 million proceeds are investing and excluded, as are acquisitions (1,248, net of cash; the Spirit AeroSystems acquisition was paid mainly in shares) and supplier notes receivable (662).

pay.notes: Employees: approximate year-end total workforce from the FY2025 10-K, which includes the employees of Spirit AeroSystems, acquired in December 2025. Payroll: the FY2025 10-K discloses no total staff cost, so the proxy's CEO pay ratio median for 2025 is used (CEO pay about 166 times the median). Boeing identifies its median employee every three years; the current one was identified in 2023 (twelve months to September 30, 2023, from about 154,360 employees), and the 16,961 Spirit AeroSystems employees were excluded.
